EnBW plans a combined cycle gas plant of about 850 MW electric on the Obrigheim nuclear site in Baden-Württemberg. Early public consultation began on July 8, 2026. EnBW lists the first round of the capacity tender in its timeline and says a decision to build depends on winning an award. An application for approval is expected in March 2027. A trade press report on the first tender round lists Obrigheim as a possible EnBW bid. GEM has no plant at Obrigheim. Recheck after the award list due by November 3, 2026.

Engie Deutschland plans a hydrogen-ready combined cycle gas plant on about 8 hectares of the former coal plant site at Ensdorf in Saarland. A news report dated June 19, 2026 says it depends on winning a federal capacity tender. A trade press report names Ensdorf as an Engie project for the first round. No capacity figure was found, so the 20 MW threshold is likely met but not confirmed. GEM has no plant at Ensdorf. Recheck after the award list due by November 3, 2026.

LEAG names Boxberg in Saxony among the coal sites where it plans new gas plants that can later run on hydrogen. A trade press report on the tender names Boxberg as one of four possible LEAG sites, but the sites with firm project names are Jänschwalde, Schwarze Pumpe, Lippendorf and Leipheim, which GEM already has. No capacity, permit or start date was found for Boxberg. Recheck after the award list due by November 3, 2026.

EdgeConneX planned eight gas engines, about 170 MW, to power its data center in Dörnigheim, Maintal near Frankfurt, because the grid connection would not arrive until 2037. After citizen protests the company dropped the gas plant and the data center is on hold since May 2026. GEM has no plant at Maintal. Record as cancelled only if a reviewer wants dropped proposals tracked. Recheck if the company finds another way to power the site.

records.plant_name: Enervie new gas plant (site not named)
records.researcher_notes: The utility Enervie in Hagen said in 2024 that it was thinking about a hydrogen-ready gas plant of up to 500 MW, depending on federal support. A trade press report from September 2026 says it has not confirmed a bid. No site, permit or date was named. GEM has the mothballed Hagen-Kabel plant, but I found nothing tying the new idea to that site. Treat as a loose lead.
